title: Jiby John vs Mincy M.L on 10 October, 2018

paragraphs.text:

 O.P.(FC) No.516 of 2018
 ------------------------------------------------
 Dated this the 10th day of October, 2018


 JUDGMENT

R.Narayana Pisharadi, J

 The petitioner is the husband and the first respondent is

 the wife.

2. The petitioner has filed O.P.No.450/2017 in the

 Family Court for granting a decree of divorce under Section

 10(1)(x) of the Divorce Act, 1869 (hereinafter referred to as

 'the Act'). The petition for divorce was filed by him on

 30.05.2016. However, in March, 2018 he filed two applications

 as I.A.Nos.1559/2018 and 1560/2018 in the Family Court. The

 application I.A.No.1559/2018 was filed for amendment of the

 petition for divorce to incorporate an averment that the first

 respondent had illicit relationship with a person by name Binu.

 The application I.A.No.1560/2018 was filed for impleading the

 aforesaid person as a co-respondent in the petition for divorce,

 on the ground that he is the adulterer.

3. The first respondent filed objection to the aforesaid
 O.P.(FC) No.516/2018
 3



 applications.

4. The Family Court dismissed both the applications

 mentioned above. The order passed by the Family Court in

 I.A.No.1560/2018 reads as follows:

"Counter filed. Heard. In the original petition
 the OP is for divorce on the ground of cruelty. A fresh
 ground of adultery and to implead additional
 respondent is not permitted in law. Hence the
 petition is dismissed."

The Family Court dismissed the application I.A.No.1559/2018

 stating as follows:

"Since the impleading petition is dismissed, I.A
 is also dismissed."

5. The aforesaid orders passed by the Family Court are

 under challenge in this Original Petition filed under Article 227 

 of the Constitution of India.
6. We have heard learned counsel for the petitioner.
7. The petition for divorce is filed under Section 10(1)

(x) of the Act on the ground of cruelty alone. Ext.P1 is the copy

 of the petition for divorce filed by the petitioner in the Family

 Court. It is specifically stated in paragraph 20 of the aforesaid

 petition that the petitioner is entitled for a decree of divorce on

 the ground of cruelty. There is no averment in the petition for
 O.P.(FC) No.516/2018
 4



 divorce that the petitioner is entitled to get a decree of divorce

 on the ground of adultery.

8. Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the

 petition for divorce is filed on the ground of adultery also. We

 do not find any substance in this submission.

9. At this juncture, we may note that in the copy of the

 petition for divorce produced before this Court as Ext.P1,

 paragraph No.19 is seen incorporated after paragraph No.13

 and paragraph Nos.14 to 18 are missing. Learned counsel for

 the petitioner has not offered any explanation for this.

10. As noticed earlier, the petition for divorce is filed

 under Section 10(1)(x) of the Act, that is, only on the ground of

 cruelty. Even if it is accepted that absence of the proper

 provision of law in the title of the petition is of no consequence,

 it is to be noted that the petition for divorce does not contain

 any averment regarding any act of adultery committed by the

 first respondent. What is stated in paragraph 12 of the petition

 for divorce is the following:

"After she left the matrimonial home on 24th
 March 2016 news spread like a wild conflagration
 that the respondent had eloped with someone.
 Speculation was agog that the respondent was
 leading a lascivious and libidinous life. More
 O.P.(FC) No.516/2018
 5


 skeletons fell out of the cupboard. The respondent
 was leading a wayward life to the knowledge of the
 entire public for a considerable period of time. The
 petitioner was shell shocked on hearing these
 scandals about the respondent."

11. The aforesaid vague averments do not amount to

 allegation of adultery against the first respondent. The first

 respondent had eloped with a person or that she was leading a

 lascivious and libidinous life or a wayward life does not

 necessarily mean that she has committed adultery.

12. In Susanta Kumar Mitra v. Himangshu Prova

 Mitra : AIR 1964 Cal 33, the Calcutta High Court has

 observed as follows:

''The learned Judge treats this petition as one
 under Section 10 of the Indian Divorce Act on
 the ground of adultery coupled with desertion
 without reasonable excuse for more than two
 years. Unfortunately he has failed to notice
 that the word "adultery" was not even alleged
 in the petition. Paragraph 5 of the petition
 says that "the respondent used to bring
 people into the house and used to pass nights
 with them". That, in our opinion is not enough
 assertion and allegation of the actual act of
 adultery".

13. There is no whisper in the petition for divorce that the

 wife has committed adultery. There is no averment in the

 petition for divorce that the wife had sexual intercourse with a

 man other than the petitioner.

14. At this juncture, we shall examine the basis on which

 the application for amendment of the petition for divorce was

 filed by the petitioner. In the affidavit filed by the petitioner in

 support of the application for amendment, it is stated in the

 third paragraph that, at the time of filing the original petition

 the petitioner had mentioned the illicit relationship of his wife

 with an autorickshaw driver by name Binu Jacob. This

 averment in the affidavit filed by the petitioner is absolutely

 incorrect, if not, false. There is no averment in the petition for

 divorce that the wife of the petitioner had illicit relationship with

 any person by name Binu Jacob. The prayer for amendment of

 the petition for divorce and impleading the person by name Binu

 as additional second respondent was made by the petitioner on

 the basis that the petition for divorce already contained

 averments as to the adultery committed by his wife. In fact,

 the petition for divorce does not contain any averment that the

 wife of the petitioner committed adultery. In these

 circumstances, the Family Court was perfectly justified in
 O.P.(FC) No.516/2018
 7



 dismissing the applications filed by the petitioner.

15. Amendment of plaint introducing a totally new case

 cannot be permitted. Amendment can be allowed to elaborate,

 explain or modify the pleadings. Normally, the right to relief

 must be judged to exist as on the date a suitor institutes the

 legal proceeding. The right of a party is determined by the facts

 as they exist on the date the action is instituted. Where a cause

 of action is deficient but later events have made up the

 deficiency, the court may, in order to avoid multiplicity of

 litigation, permit amendment and continue the proceeding,

 provided no prejudice is caused to the other side (See

 Rameshwar v. Jot Ram : AIR 1976 SC 49). The position of law,

 therefore, seems to be that divorce on the ground of adultery

 could be allowed to be incorporated in the petition subsequently

 by amendment provided the ground existed at the time of filing

 of the petition.

16. In the instant case, the attempt of the petitioner is to

 seek a relief of divorce on an additional ground of adultery by

 amendment of the petition for divorce. By amendment of the

 petition for divorce, the petitioner seeks to introduce a totally

 new case and new ground for divorce. True, the amendment will

 not change the nature and character of the suit or the relief.
 O.P.(FC) No.516/2018
 8



 But, a totally new cause of action for seeking divorce is sought

 to be introduced by way of amendment which is not

 permissible. It is significant that the petitioner has no case that

 he came to know about the act of adultery allegedly committed

 by his wife only about two years after the filing of the petition

 for divorce.

17. In the aforesaid circumstances, we find no ground to

 interfere with the impugned orders passed by the Family Court.
Consequently, we dismiss the Original Petition.

(sd/-)

 C.K.ABDUL REHIM, JUDGE

 (sd/-)

 R.NARAYANA PISHARADI, JUDGE
